attributes.axis_log: A1 ARITHMETIC PREDICTION BEFORE EDITING (the required discipline): 25 SWAP16 + 7 SWAP32 + 38 SWAPF textual expansion sites, costed at world.c's proven helper frames (u16 helper 4, u32 helper 8, f32 helper nesting the u32 helper 16) = 25*4 + 7*8 + 38*16 = 764. Target low_gap measured 776; ours 624. A2 converted all 70 sites mechanically to `x = sSwapU16(x)` form with world.c's exact helper bodies and deleted the surplus `volatile u8 unused[600]` hand pad a prior pass had added -> real 1635 -> 1344 BUT insns collapsed 1139 -> 516 with `ours-only -70 bl`: the helpers were emitted as REAL CALLS, not inlined, because `#pragma dont_inline on` bracketed LoadPlyrData. A3 lifted that pragma pair -> helpers inlined, real 1344 -> 465, insns 1138/1179, and the frame closed EXACTLY: target frame 1568 / low_gap 776 vs ours frame 1568 / low_gap 776, calls 15/15. COMMITTED at this state (gate: 1 improved, 0 regressions; full ninja + main.dol sha1 OK). A4 the remaining 78 real diffs were then localised by aligned fnasm read to ONE mechanism: the target keeps `bl PlayerSfxInitData` while our build now inlines PlayerSfxInitData's record-clearing loop and calls only its inner fn_8008A678 - i.e. the lifted pragma was load-bearing for that call. Three distinct forms were tried to get BOTH inlined helpers and a real PlayerSfxInitData call, all rejected: A4a `#pragma dont_inline on/off` around PlayerSfxInitData's own DEFINITION (the idiom this TU already uses for PlayerSfxClearData) -> LoadPlyrData real 387 but PlayerSfxInitData EXACT -> OPERAND_DIFF, its own frame growing 48 -> 56; two compensation sub-probes (drop 2 locals -> frame 48 but one `addi` copy where target rematerializes `li`; restore secondOff -> opcode multiset IDENTICAL 33/33 but frame back to 56 with an r30/r31 bijection) never recovered exactness, and regressing an exact sibling is barred by the mandate. A4b `#pragma dont_inline on` placed INSIDE LoadPlyrData's body immediately before the resolve tail -> REFUTED, see the law this attempt authors: the pragma governed the whole function, helpers returned to 70 bl and were emitted standalone. A4c `#pragma always_inline on` around the three helpers combined with `dont_inline on` around LoadPlyrData -> byte-identical to A4b, always_inline does NOT override dont_inline. Axis capped at three distinct forms per the per-axis dead-end rule; tree restored to the A3 commit and re-gated GATE OK.

attributes.residual: IMPROVED, not exact. Best retained: real 465 (from 1635), insns 1138/1179, frame and low_gap now EXACT at 1568/776. The entire remaining residual is ONE named mechanism: MWCC inlines PlayerSfxInitData (defined at psfx.c:1070, before the call sites) into LoadPlyrData, where the target emits `bl PlayerSfxInitData`. This is NOT reachable while the swap helpers must inline, because `#pragma dont_inline` is function-granular (see claim.law.dont-inline-pragma-is-function-granular-and-unoverridable.20260831.v1, authored by this attempt): one pragma cannot both force a call and permit helper inlining inside the same function. Definition-order reordering (the other lever in claim.law.inline-and-deadstrip-rules) is barred here because .text order must match the target and fn_8008A678 must stay defined AFTER PlayerSfxInitData. The untried levers for a future pass are: (1) a source form for PlayerSfxInitData that MWCC's inliner declines on its own merits without a pragma and without changing its emitted bytes; (2) a WebFrank rule if the residual reduces to a clean bijection. MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION: the frame-bottom measure used here is min(referenced r1 displacement) - 8 over memory displacements plus `addi rX,r1,N` and `mr rX,r1`; it resolves 4 bytes and cannot see reservations that are read by no instruction and alias an existing slot.
